correctness.rationale: For a selected vertex in part i the representation contains one 0, |W|-w_i ones and w_i-1 twos; for an unselected vertex it contains |W|-w_i ones and w_i twos. Across parts, selected-selected and unselected-unselected representations collide exactly at equal corresponding occupancies, while selected-unselected representations cannot collide because only the former contains 0. Hence positive occupancies must be pairwise distinct and at most one zero is allowed. Any valid profile therefore has at least r-1 distinct positive integers and size at least 1+...+(r-1). Such a minimum profile is feasible exactly when, after omitting one part, capacities can host 1,...,r-1; sorting shows this is equivalent to a_i>=i-1 for i>=2, with omitting a smallest part optimal. Summing binomial choices over every feasible permutation yields the basis count. The frozen verifier exhausts all isomorphism types through order nine but is only corroborative.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical diameter-two family for a recently developed distance-multiset invariant. The theorem completely resolves existence, the exact minimum, every minimum occupancy profile, and the number of bases for arbitrary part sizes. This is a natural family classification rather than an arbitrary finite exercise.

final_claim: For G=K_{n_1,...,n_r}, W is local multiset resolving iff at most one part has zero selected vertices and all positive selected part counts are pairwise distinct; after sorting part sizes a_1<=...<=a_r, finiteness is equivalent to a_i>=i-1 for i=2,...,r, then lmd(G)=binomial(r,2), with the stated exact basis-count sum over feasible permutations of 0,...,r-1.

The theorem concerns the local multiset invariant, not global multiset or outer variants.
